title: Static and instance members of a click counter

blocks.text: A static field belongs to the class, so every object shares it; an instance field belongs to one object. A static method is called on the class (`Counter.total()`) and cannot touch instance fields; an instance method is called on an object (`c.click()`) and can use both.
Complete `Counter`. Each counter counts its own clicks, and the class keeps a running total of the clicks of every counter:

items: `click()` adds one click to this counter, and to the total;
`Counter.total()` returns the clicks of all counters together;
`Counter.resetTotal()` sets the total back to `0` (tests call it first).

blocks.text: Example: after `a.click(); a.click(); b.click();`, `a.count()` is `2`, `b.count()` is `1` and `Counter.total()` is `3`.

cases.says: One counter clicked three times counts 3, and so does the total.
Two counters keep separate counts: count is an instance field.
Clicks on two counters add up in the total, and resetting it keeps each count.

concepts: A static method and a static field belong to the class, while an instance method works on one object's own fields.
